population.span: We enrolled 7868 women between the ages of 60 and 90 years who had a bone mineral density T score of less than -2.5 but not less than -4.0 at the lumbar spine or total hip.

endpoint.span: Secondary end points included nonvertebral and hip fractures.

estimate.span: Denosumab reduced the risk of hip fracture, with a cumulative incidence of 0.7% in the denosumab group, versus 1.2% in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.37 to 0.97; P=0.04)

analysis_set.span: Hip fractures are a subset of nonvertebral fractures including femur neck, femur intertrochanter, and femur subtrochanter. | TIME FRAME: 36 months | POPULATION: Full analysis set

treatment_strategy.span: Subjects were randomly assigned to receive either 60 mg of denosumab or placebo subcutaneously every 6 months for 36 months.

follow_up.span: Hip fractures are a subset of nonvertebral fractures including femur neck, femur intertrochanter, and femur subtrochanter. | TIME FRAME: 36 months

entry_population_matches_question.why: Women aged 60-90 with BMD T score < -2.5 (osteoporosis) in a trial titled for postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, randomised denosumab vs placebo.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Denosumab for prevention of fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

notes: Served HR 0.6 (0.37-0.97) equals the abstract's HR 0.60 (0.37 to 0.97) for hip fracture.
